title: Personal Representative
about: Records who the law lets act for a patient on health care and health information, and the papers that show it. HIPAA, 45 CFR 164.502(g); identity and authority checked under 164.514(h).

source.name: HIPAA personal representatives, 45 CFR 164.502(g), and verification, 164.514(h)

licence.terms: CC0 1.0: dedicated to the public domain. Use and adapt it freely, with no credit needed.

blocks.text: A personal representative is someone the law lets make health care decisions for the patient. Within that authority, we treat them as the patient for the patient's health information.
This is often a health care power of attorney, a guardian, the parent of a child, or the person in charge of the estate of someone who has died.

blocks.label: Their legal authority (tick one)
items: Health care power of attorney or health care agent
Guardian or conservator named by a court
Parent or legal guardian of a minor child
Executor or administrator of the estate of a patient who has died

blocks.label: Other authority, and any limits on it

blocks.text: Please bring a copy of the paper that gives this authority, such as the power of attorney or the court order. We keep a copy in the patient's record.
For a child, some care the child can agree to alone may stay private, as state law allows. Then the parent may not see those records.
If you only want us to talk with a family member or friend, you do not need this form: use our Communication Preferences form. To send records to someone, use our Release of Information form.
